result.title: Clustering-Based Artificial Tree Ensembles for Random Forest Approximation
result.summary: Random Forests (RFs) offer strong prediction performance but are difficult to interpret. Most representative trees (MRTs) and artificial representative trees (ARTs) provide surrogate explanations, but a single tree may miss patterns within a forest. We investigate benefits and limitations of clustering-based representative tree ensembles for RF surrogate modeling and assess the contribution of similarity-based clustering relative to random tree partitions. Using linear and nonlinear simulations and regression benchmarks, we evaluate fidelity, prediction accuracy, complexity, and prediction stability against equally sized ensembles of top-ranked MRTs and randomly selected trees. Increasing ensemble size generally improves fidelity, accuracy, and prediction stability. ART ensembles show higher fidelity in simulations and often greater prediction stability for small ensembles. Compared with random tree partitions, similarity-based clustering generally improves ART fidelity in simulations and often on benchmarks. On benchmark datasets, MRT-based ensembles generally achieve higher fidelity and prediction accuracy, whereas ART ensembles have fewer terminal nodes. ART ensembles provide compact surrogates when reduced complexity matters and their fidelity and prediction accuracy meet application requirements. These findings clarify both the trade-offs of representative tree ensembles as RF surrogates and the contribution of similarity-based clustering beyond random clustering.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究以聚类得到的代表性树集成作为随机森林的替代模型，在模拟与回归基准上比较其保真度、预测精度、复杂度与稳定性，并考察相似度聚类相对随机划分的增量贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相似度聚类选择代表成员并对照随机划分、评估保真度与复杂度权衡」的实验范式，可能可供核查 latent 假设或推理轨迹的聚类筛选是否真有增益，但与 VLM 内部状态和推理决策尚无实质联系。
